title: Rav Shimi of Nehardea
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bava Kamma 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.32b.10-13): Rava objected—Rav Shimi of Neharde'a said that they erred in the count; Rava struck him with his sandal and said to him: Is he the one who counts? etc.

In [Shevuot 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.12b.1-2) (Hyman’s print cites Sheviit 12b), Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak tells Rava, “I said it in Rav Shimi of Nehardea’s name.” Hyman infers that Shimi was something like Rava’s colleague.

He is also mentioned in [Berakhot 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.36b.9), [Pesachim 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.52b.11), [Yoma 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.6a.11), [Bava Kamma 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.26a.15), and [Makkot 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.16a.14-15).

[Eruvin 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.25a.7) has Rav Shimi explaining Rabbah and Rava’s disagreement. [Megillah 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.21b.8) has “Rav Shimi taught”; Hyman says it is possible that he is R’ Shimi of Nehardea.
In [Zevachim 71b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.71b.10) Rav Ashi says: “I recited the teaching before Rav Shimi [of Nehardea, according to Dikdukei Soferim].”[^4]

notes.text: Hyman supplies שביעית, Sheviit, at 12b, while the earlier English substituted Shevuot. The source reference remains flagged rather than silently corrected. The bracketed Nehardea specification is attributed to Dikdukei Soferim.

The whole saved Davidson Shevuot 12b scalar 1 has full Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak speaking to Rava and full Rav Shimi of Nehardea as reported authority. Supplied שביעית12b is retained beside the named Shevuot match, without a categorical print-slip history. Hyman’s something-like-a-colleague inference and possible Eruvin/Megillah identity remain his. The other bare folio numbers receive no invented sides. The Zevachim Nehardea phrase remains bracketed as supplied and attributed to Dikdukei Soferim; this work’s text was not freshly inspected. Source full Rav Ashi and Rav Shimi are preserved.

Hyman’s print (III, p. 1116) gives Sheviit 12b for the exchange found at Shevuot 12b. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says that he passed on the teaching in Rav Shimi of Nehardea’s name. In Bava Kamma 32b, the senior judge reads, the second counts, and the third tells the attendant when to strike. After Rava’s objection, Shimi says that the judge himself miscounted. The consulted folios listed in the article name Shimi of Nehardea, with Makkot 16a distinguishing him from Shimi of Mechoza in the preceding statement. Eruvin 25a, Megillah 21b, and Zevachim 71b give Rav Shimi without a place name. Hyman’s bracketed Nehardea in Zevachim is his reported Dikdukei Soferim reading.

Bava Kamma distinguishes the judge who counts from the attendant who strikes. Shimi’s final answer is that the judge miscounted. The consulted Shevuot gives the transmission from Shimi of Nehardea. In Makkot the preceding statement belongs to Shimi of Mechoza; only the next one gives Nehardea.
